relevance_note: This single-centre thalidomide cohort of 16 children with monogenic autoinflammatory diseases includes two HA20 patients with individual-level detail in the supplementary table, e.g. case 12 "TNFAIP3: p. R271X" and case 13 "TNFAIP3: p. D70N".
method_note: Read the whole paper, including the supplementary material (MOESM1 disease-activity definitions; MOESM2 per-patient table), and built the JSON with a small Python script. Every value was entered by hand from my reading; the script only assembles the rows and checks the spans verbatim. Scope: 16 patients in the study (cohort_size_as_stated), and only cases 12 and 13 (HA20, TNFAIP3) are in scope; the 14 patients with other monogenic AIDs get no rows. Labels: the paper refers to its patients as 'Case 1', 'Cases 4 and 6', 'cases 4,12,13', 'cases 5 and 12', and its tables number them in a 'No' column, so I used 'Case 12' and 'Case 13'. Two previously published HA20 patients from reference [17] (PMID:34030699) are described in the Discussion ('both showed amelioration of gastrointestinal symptoms... and eventually discontinued glucocorticoid therapy'), so I gave them rows 'ref [17] patient' and 'ref [17] patient 2'. The paper prints no variant and names no gene for them, so they have no variant rows. Their checklist is all 'not reported', because 'gastrointestinal symptoms' does not establish ulcers or inflammation. Table 1 has disease groups as columns, and HA20 is the 6th data column, after AGS, Blau syndrome, CINCA, DADA2 and FMF. Its legend defines each cell as the number of positive cases in that disease category. For the six manifestation rows where the HA20 cell is 0 (growth or intellectual disability, cardiovascular, joint, eye or ear, hematologic, neurologic), I marked the feature excluded for both HA20 patients, with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'. Non-zero HA20 counts that cannot be tied to one patient were not used: elevated CRP 1, elevated ESR 1, respiratory 1. So 'elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR)' is 'not reported' for both patients, although one of the two had elevated CRP and one had elevated ESR at baseline. Cardiovascular involvement 0 was not used to exclude 'pericarditis or other serositis' or 'vasculitis', because those are broader or different composite items. 'Peripheral neuropathy' and 'somnolence' are marked excluded for both from 'None of the patients had adverse events such as...'. The study's exclusion criteria (liver dysfunction, neuropathy) were not used as evidence. Case 12 has 'hypothyroidism', which I did not map to the checklist item 'autoimmune thyroiditis' (left 'not reported'). Case 12's 'multiple nodules in both lungs' was not mapped to interstitial lung disease. Case 12's anorexia and nausea are thalidomide adverse events. They are recorded as observed features, with the dose context in severity_or_detail. 'Recurrent fever' is marked observed for both: the per-patient table lists 'Fever', Table 1 has HA20 fever 2, and the text calls the cohort's 8 febrile patients 'recurrent fevers (8, 50.0%)'. The supplementary table gives age at baseline (start of thalidomide): 11.50 years for case 12 and 5.75 years for case 13. Patients were followed for 12 months after baseline, so this is not the age at last evaluation, and the schema has no baseline-age field. I left the ages 'not reported' and give them here. Variants are printed protein-only ('p. R271X', 'p. D70N', with a space after 'p.'), with no transcript, zygosity, inheritance or classification, so those fields are not reported. Table 1 HA20 pre-thalidomide treatment counts: glucocorticoids 0, immunosuppressive agents 1, others 1 (hydroxychloroquine). The last two cannot be attributed to either patient and were left out of treatment_summary. Table 2 HA20 scores use the HA20 severity scale defined in MOESM1 (mild, moderate, severe). Inconsistencies noticed: (a) the Discussion says the 2 patients with side effects had 'nausea, fatigue, and anorexia', but the Results give only anorexia and nausea for cases 5 and 12; fatigue was not recorded for case 12. (b) The Results say ESR 'reached the normal ranges' in '16 patients (100.0%)' at 3 months, although only nine had elevated ESR at baseline. This does not affect individual rows. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null: the paper does not state that cases 12 or 13 were described before.
